Effects of Digital Transformation in Manufacturing SMEs: Focusing on the Paths of Innovation Activity, Innovation Capability, and Innovation Performance

Hwang, Young Soon . Ha, Sung Ho

Purpose This study  empirically analyzes how  digital  transformation (DX)  influences  the  structural

relationship between innovation activities, capabilities, and performance in manufacturing SMEs.

It identifies the moderating and moderated mediation effects of DX across small and large-scale

SMEs to provide strategic insights for maximizing innovation outcomes.

Design/methodology/approach
Using 2022 Korean Innovation Survey (KIS) microdata from 1,597 SMEs, the sample was

clustered  into small-scale (n=854) and  large-scale (n=743) groups. Hayes’ PROCESS Macro

(Models 1 and 59) was applied to rigorously test moderated mediation effects across structural paths

while controlling for industry-specific variables.

Findings Results reveal size-dependent innovation paths: small-scale SMEs thrive through “new product

launches” and “quality” via DX-driven capabilities, while large-scale SMEs excel in “customer

acquisition” and “price competitiveness” with DX support. Although innovation capability is a

universal driver, DX's role as a catalyst varies by scale, necessitating tailored DX strategies aligned

with organizational size to secure competitive advantages.

Keyword: Digital  Transformation,  Innovation  Activities,  Innovation  Capabilities,  Innovation Performance, SME

Effects of Digital Transformation in Manufacturing SMEs: Focusing on the Paths of Innovation Activity, Innovation Capability, and Innovation Performance

Hwang, Young Soon . Ha, Sung Ho

Purpose This study  empirically analyzes how  digital  transformation (DX)  influences  the  structural

relationship between innovation activities, capabilities, and performance in manufacturing SMEs.

It identifies the moderating and moderated mediation effects of DX across small and large-scale

SMEs to provide strategic insights for maximizing innovation outcomes.

sections.title: Design/methodology/approach
sections.content:
Using 2022 Korean Innovation Survey (KIS) microdata from 1,597 SMEs, the sample was

clustered  into small-scale (n=854) and  large-scale (n=743) groups. Hayes’ PROCESS Macro

(Models 1 and 59) was applied to rigorously test moderated mediation effects across structural paths

while controlling for industry-specific variables.

Findings Results reveal size-dependent innovation paths: small-scale SMEs thrive through “new product

launches” and “quality” via DX-driven capabilities, while large-scale SMEs excel in “customer

acquisition” and “price competitiveness” with DX support. Although innovation capability is a

universal driver, DX's role as a catalyst varies by scale, necessitating tailored DX strategies aligned

with organizational size to secure competitive advantages.

Keyword: Digital  Transformation,  Innovation  Activities,  Innovation  Capabilities,  Innovation Performance, SME
